question: What minimum sight distance for signal visibility does Table 4D-2 list at an 85th-percentile speed of 45 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Table 4D-2 lists a minimum sight distance of 460 feet for an 85th-percentile speed of 45 mph. This is the distance over which the two primary signal faces should be continuously visible in advance of (and measured to) the stop line; the table's note states the values are derived from stopping sight distance plus an assumed queue length for shorter cycle lengths (60 to 75 seconds). Guidance (recommended): - "The two primary signal faces required as a minimum for each approach should be continuously visible to traffic approaching the traffic control signal, from a point at least the minimum sight distance provided in Table 4D-2 in advance of and measured to the stop line. This range of continuous visibility should be provided unless precluded by a physical obstruction or unless another signalized location is within this range." - "If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for at least the minimum sight distance shown in Table 4D-2, a sign (see Section 2C.35) should be installed to warn approaching traffic of the traffic control signal." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 4D-2, "Minimum Sight Distance for Signal Visibility," with the row for 45 mph listing 460 feet. [Image 2] shows the full page 670 containing Section 4D.06 and Table 4D-2, confirming the 45 mph / 460 feet entry and the derivation note. Citations: - Table 4D-2 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §5 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §6 (p.670)
